s: What are the provisions of the directive principles under Article 45 of our constitution? Note: For this question, discrepancy is found in question / answer. So, this question is ignored for all candidates.
o: Provide free and compulsory education to all children till the age of 14 years
Provide free food and shelter to all children till the age of 14 years
Promote the welfare of all people including disabled
ensure that all citizens have the right to an adequate means of livelihood
src: APPSC Group-2 PYQ
x: APPSC withdrew this question (discrepancy). The current Art. 45 provides early childhood care and education for all children until they complete six years; option 1 (education till 14) is the pre-2002 text, so no option states the present provision.

s: The child labour was prohibited in hazardous employment by–
o: The judgment of Supreme Court on December 10,
src: U.P. Lower Sub. (Spl) (Pre) 2003 +1 more
x: Defective: child labour in hazardous work is prohibited by the Constitution (Art. 24) and by the SC judgment of 10 Dec 1996 (M.C. Mehta v. State of T.N.), but the UN Charter (1945) says nothing on child labour (that is the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, 1989), so 'All of the above' is not strictly correct and no 'both' option exists. (Official key: All of the above.)

s:
Freedom under Constitution of India is subject to

I. public order, morality and health.

II. a law providing for social welfare and reform.

III. opening Hindu religious institutions of a public character to all Hindus.

IV. defamation or incitement to an offence.
Which of the above statements are correct?
src: CDS 2015
x: Art. 25 is subject to public order, morality and health (I), and to laws for social welfare and reform and opening Hindu public religious institutions to all Hindus (II, III). Defamation/incitement is an Art. 19 ground, not Art. 25.

s: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution provides freedom to practice any religion to Indian citizens?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I, Assistant Public Relation,
x: Article 25 gives freedom to profess, practise and propagate religion (to all persons, citizens included).

s: The Right of Property ceased to be a Fundamental Right from
src: APPSC MPDO 1998
x:
Most books and exam keys give 1978, the year of the 44th Amendment Act. Strictly, Article 31 was deleted with effect from 20 June 1979, when that part of the Act came into force.
The 44th Amendment Act is 'of 1978', but it got assent on 30 April 1979 and the omission of Art. 31 took effect on 20 June 1979, so property ceased to be an FR from 1979 (printed key: 1978).

s: Which of the following is a judicial writ issued as a command to an inferior court or ordering a person to perform a public or statutory duty?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) 2
x: Mandamus commands an inferior court or a person to perform a public or statutory duty.

s: Which of the following right is described by Dr. B.R.Ambedkar as 'The Heart and soul of the Constitution'?
src: Deputy Information Engineers & in Sector of Boilers 2019
x: Ambedkar called the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Art. 32) the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

s: Which of the following Article enables High court to issue writs?
src: Assistant Executive Electrical Engineering 2019
x: Article 226 empowers the High Courts to issue writs.

s: Directive Principles of State Policy are enumerated in which part of the Indian Constitution?
src: APPSC Group-IV (Hostel Welfare Officers) 2012
x: DPSPs are in Part IV (Articles 36-51).

s: Which part of the constitution of India deals with Directive Principles of State Policy?
src: APPSC Wardens Grade-I & III 2012
x: The DPSPs are in Part IV (Arts. 36-51); Part III is FRs, Part II citizenship and Part V the Union.

s: They are not enforceable by the Courts. 2. It shall be the duty of the State to apply these Principles in making laws. Select the correct answer using the code given below : Code-
src: UP R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2023
x: Both are the words of Art. 37: not enforceable by courts, yet the State has a duty to apply them in making laws.

s: Who said that Directive Principles of the State Policy was 'New Magna Carta'?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
x: No authority settles who called the DPSPs a 'New Magna Carta'. Vijeta's answer grid prints '1,3' (M.V. Pylee and Ambedkar). Part III (the FRs) is the part usually called India's 'Magna Carta', and Part IV is called a 'socio-economic Magna Carta' only without a named author. The question stays unkeyed.

s: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 has inserted in the Constitution of India a new Article
src: APPSC Technical Asst. in Archaeology & Museums 2012
x: The 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Art. 21A (Right to Education), substituted Art. 45 and added duty 51A(k).

s:
Consider the following statements with respect to 'The 61st Constitutional Amendment':

b. It was introduced by B. Shankaranand in the Lok Sabha on 13 December 1988, as the Constitution (Sixty-second Amendment) Bill, 1988.
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Both are correct: the 61st Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18, and it was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 13 December 1988 by B. Shankaranand as the Constitution (Sixty-second Amendment) Bill, 1988. (Printed answer: neither a nor b.)

s: Following Constitutional amendment Acts were declared as unconstitutional, except
src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
x: Struck down (wholly or partly): 25th (second part of Art. 31C, Kesavananda), 32nd (Art. 371D(5), Sambamurthy 1987). Neither the 7th nor the 12th Amendment was ever declared unconstitutional, so two options fit 'except' – question defective.

s: Who among the following proposed the theory of 'Civil Legitimacy'?
src: Civil Services (Preliminary) 2000
x: Unkeyed: 'civil legitimacy' is not a standard theory name. Hobbes, Locke and Rousseau all grounded the legitimacy of civil government in a social contract, and no source attributes the phrase to one of them, so no option can be fixed.

s: President addressed joint session of two houses of Indian Parliament on
src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers 2019
x: President Pratibha Patil addressed the joint session of Parliament opening the Budget Session on 12 March 2012. (President; moved.)

s: The term 'cabinet' is mentioned in which of the following articles of constitution?
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: The word 'cabinet' occurs only once in the Constitution, in Article 352(3) (inserted by the 44th Amendment, 1978), which requires the Union Cabinet's written advice for a National Emergency. Arts. 74-75 speak of the Council of Ministers.

s: Which of the following states has the maximum Rajya Sabha seats?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I, Assistant Public Relation,
x: Uttar Pradesh has the most Rajya Sabha seats (31). The printed answer 'Andhra Pradesh' could only hold before 2014 for a paper whose options left out UP and Maharashtra (undivided AP had 18, equal to Tamil Nadu); AP now has 11.

s: Which of the following states has the maximum Lok Sabha seats?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I, Assistant Public Relation,
x: Uttar Pradesh has the most Lok Sabha seats (80), followed by Maharashtra (48) – the printed answer 'Maharashtra' is wrong.

s: The President of India cannot dissolve this House
src: Grama/Ward Sachivalayam 2019 Village Agriculture Assistant (
x: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House not subject to dissolution; the President can dissolve the Lok Sabha (and, on the Governor's side, Assemblies are dissolved by the Governor).

s:
With reference to Lok Sabha, which of the following statements is/are correct?

a. The Lok Sabha was duly constituted for the first time on 17th April, 1952 after the first General Elections held from 25th October, 1951 to 21st February, 1952.

b. The 1st Lok Sabha lasted its full tenure of five years and was dissolved on 4th May, 1957.

c. The first Session of the first Lok Sabha commenced on 13th April, 1952.
src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Divisional Account Officer Screening
x: Only a is right: the 1st LS was constituted on 17 April 1952 after polls of 25 Oct 1951 – 21 Feb 1952. It was dissolved on 4 April 1957 (not 4 May) and its first session began on 13 May 1952 (not 13 April).

s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about Zero Hour?

1. Zero Hour has special provision mentioned in the rule of procedure

2. India has adopted Zero Hour from UK

3. Zero Hour starts immediately after the Question Hour and lasts until the agenda from the day is taken up

4. Before raising question in Zero Hour the members of parliament required to give prior notice
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x:
Most books and keys: no prior notice (3 only). Strictly: Lok Sabha members now give same-day notices, which are balloted before the sitting (Lok Sabha Bulletin Part II).
Only 3 is correct: Zero Hour starts right after Question Hour and lasts until the agenda is taken up. It is not in the Rules (1 wrong), it is an Indian innovation (2 wrong), and it needs no advance notice like a question (4 wrong)

s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the Governor?

a. He can nominate one member to the state legislature assembly from the Anglo Indian Community.

b. He can seek any information relating to the administration of the affairs of the state and proposals for legislation from the Chief Minister.

c. A person completed the age of 30 can be appointed as governor.

d. The governor acts as agent of the central government.
src: Assistant Executive Electrical Engineering 2019
x:
Anglo-Indian nomination to State Assemblies (Art. 333) ended on 25 January 2020 under the 104th Amendment — now only (b) is correct (Constitution (104th Amendment) Act, 2019)
In 2019 (a) and (b) were correct: the Governor nominated one Anglo-Indian to the Assembly (Art. 333) (now ended – 25 Jan 2020, 104th Amendment) and can seek information from the CM (Art. 167). The minimum age is 35, not 30, a

src: U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2015 +1 more

s:
Consider the following statements in respect to 'Justice Malimath Committee':

b. The Committee suggested constituting a National Judicial Commission and amending Article 124 to make impeachment of judges less difficult.

src: Assistant BC, Social, Tribal Welfare Officer Screening Test
x: Only b: the Malimath Committee (2003) was on criminal justice reform, not Panchayati Raj; it suggested a National Judicial Commission and amending Art. 124 to ease impeachment of judges.

s: In the context of establishing a new High Court of the state, which of the following statement is correct?
at: The President of India, after the authorization by the Parliament, through a notification can create new High Court for a state.
src: Jr. Assistant Computer Assistant in ANGRAU 2019
x: A new HC is created by a law of Parliament (Art. 231 / reorganisation Acts) and is brought into being by a Presidential notification – e.g. the AP HC from 1 Jan 2019.

s: The Central Administrative Tribunal was formed on
src: APSLPRB SI Prelims Paper-II 2016
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (1-11-1985); it is added as option 5.
None of the printed dates is right: the Central Government established the CAT with effect from 1 November 1985 under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 (official key: 2-10-1985). The year 1985 is right; 2 October is not the date, and 1983, 1984 and 1986 are wrong years.

s: President of India declared National Emergency ..... times till now.
src: APPSC AMVI, AEs & Observers (Non-Engg.) 2013

src: UPPSC (Mains) 2010
x: A federal polity covers Union-State relations, inter-State relations and mechanisms both for cooperation and for settling disputes – all four (options 2 and 3 are printed identically).

s: Which one of the following does not come under all India services ?
src: APPSC AP Municipal Junior Accounts Officers 2012
x: Only three All India Services exist – IAS, IPS and the Indian Forest Service. The Indian Economic Service and Indian Statistical Service are Central Services and there is no 'Indian Defence Service' AIS, so three of the four options are correct and the question has no single answer (likely misprinted options).

s:
Consider the following statements in respect of financial emergency under Article 360 of the Constitution of India:

a. A proclamation of financial emergency issued shall cease to operate at the expiration of two months, unless before the expiration of that period it has been approved by the resolutions of both Houses of Parliament.

b. If any proclamation of financial emergency is in operation it is competent for the President of India to issue directions for the reduction of salaries and allowances of all or any class of persons serving in connection with the affairs of the Union but excluding the Judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
src: Assistant Executive Electrical Engineering 2019
x: Statement a is right – a Financial Emergency lapses after two months unless both Houses approve it. b is wrong – salary cuts can extend to the Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.

s: National Emergency was declared in India under Article 352, till now ____ times.
src: APPSC Technical Asst. in Archaeology & Museums 2012
x: National Emergency has been proclaimed three times – 1962, 1971 and 1975.

s:
Consider the following statements:

a. Election Commission was a single member body from 1950 to 1989.

b. A person convicted of any offence & sentenced to an imprisonment of two years or more cannot contest elections.

c. A person confined in jail can vote in an election.
at: Only c is incorrect (a and b are correct)
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: a is true: the ECI was single-member until October 1989. b is true: a sentence of 2 years or more disqualifies (Sec. 8(3) RPA 1951). c is false: a person confined in prison cannot vote (Sec. 62(5) RPA 1951; only preventive detenus vote by postal ballot). So 'Only c' answers the 'incorrect' form of the question.

s:
Which of the following statement is/are incorrect about Election Commission of India?

a. Election Commission of India conducts elections for Lok Sabha, Vidhan Sabha and Gram Sabha.

b. Election Commission of India conducts elections only for Lok Sabha.

c. Election Commission of India conducts elections only for Vidhan Sabha.

d. Election Commission of India conducts elections for only Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha.
at: All four (a, b, c, d) are incorrect – deleted in the official key
src: Assistant Executive Electrical Engineering 2019
x: The ECI does not hold Gram Sabha/panchayat polls (State Election Commissions do) and it conducts Lok Sabha, Assembly, Rajya Sabha, Council, President and VP elections, so every statement is incorrect; the official key deleted the question.

s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding Exit Poll with respect to Lok Sabha election 2019?

a. Exit Poll is a poll of voters taken immediately after they have exited the polling stations.

b. Exit Polls and Opinion Polls are one and the same.

c. Exit polls can only be telecasted after the last phase of election gets over.

d. Usually private companies working for newspapers or broadcasters conduct exit polls.
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: An exit poll surveys voters just after they leave the booth (a), is barred till half an hour after the last phase (Sec. 126A) (c) and is run by private agencies (d); an opinion poll is a pre-poll survey, so b is wrong.

s:
Regarding National Electoral Transformation (NETA) Application, sometimes seen in the news, which of the following statements is/are correct?

a. It has been conceptualized and developed by the Election Commission of India.

b. It allows voters to rate and review their political representatives.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: The NETA app lets voters rate their representatives (b), but it was built by a private start-up, not the ECI (a is wrong).

s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about NOTA?

a. NOTA was first used in the India in 2009, but made its debut in Assembly elections in 2013.

b. NOTA has its own symbol, "A ballot paper with a black cross across it".

c. NOTA is available only for direct elections such as the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, not for Rajya Sabha and the Legislative Council.

d. Whether NOTA gets more or less votes, it is not taken into account for calculating the total valid votes.
at: b, c and d (a is wrong)
src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Divisional Account Officer Screening
x: a is wrong: NOTA came only after the SC's PUCL judgment (27 Sept 2013) and was first used in the Nov-Dec 2013 Assembly polls (not in 2009). b, c, d are true: symbol = ballot with a black cross (NID), not for Rajya Sabha/Councils (SC 2018), NOTA votes are not counted as valid votes for deposits/results.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the VVPAT (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trial) machines used by Election Commission of India?

a. VVPAT system gives instant feedback to the voter showing that the vote polled has in fact been allotted against the candidate chosen.

b. A voter-verified paper audit trial was first used in an election in India in 2013 in Nagaland.

c. A printed VVPAT slip is displayed for 30 seconds before it is automatically cut and delivered to a sealed ballot compartment.
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: a and b are correct: the VVPAT slip gives the voter instant feedback, and it was first used in the Noksen (Nagaland) by-election in 2013. c is wrong – the slip is displayed for 7 seconds, not 30.

s:
Which of the following is amongst the criteria for being registered as a national political party?

a. It is recognized as a recognized political party in 2 or more states.

b. At the last general election to the house of people, the party has won at least 5% of the total number of seats.
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: Neither is a criterion: a party needs recognition in four States (not two), or 2% of Lok Sabha seats (11) from three States (not 5% of seats), or 6% votes in four States plus 4 Lok Sabha seats.

s: According to Comptroller and Auditor General of India report, which of the following is true in relation to the composition of total revenue receipts of Andhra Pradesh in 2015-16 Financial Year?

src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: The CAG's State Finances Audit Report for AP 2015-16 shows the State's own tax revenue (about Rs 39,900 crore) at around 45% of revenue receipts (about Rs 88,600 crore).

s: Which of the following statement is true in relation to India's Five year plans?
at: In the initial years of planning, the five years plans have kept the market economy at bay
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: The early Five-Year Plans gave the State and public sector the commanding heights and kept the market economy at bay until the 1991 reforms.

s: Which of the following hub of NITI Aayog leads the engagement of states with central government?

s:

Using the codes given below, select the correct answer.
src: Civil Services (Preliminary) 1999
x: Defective: the pairs are garbled and no key can be verified. Gotra = lineage (exogamous descent from a common ancestor) is the only clearly right pair; 'marriage–group', 'family–organization' and 'tribe–complex' have no standard meaning, so the printed 'B, C, D' cannot be confirmed.

s: Who among the following is secondary kin?
src: APPSC Sociology Back Log 2000
x: The translated options are garbled: B (sisters' husbands) and D (wife's brothers) both list only secondary kin, while C mixes a primary kin (younger brother) with a secondary one (elder brother's wife) and A mixes tertiary and secondary kin, so no single option can be keyed (printed key: C).

s: Which of the following States has the lowest concentration of tribal population?
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: Tripura has about 32% STs (Census 2011), the lowest share among the North-Eastern tribal States, which are tribal-majority (Mizoram, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Arunachal). If Assam were an option it would be lower (about 12%); the app shows no options.

s: Which of the following is not a source of social change?
at: Migration of nomads in a particular season
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: Seasonal migration of nomads is a routine, recurring cycle, so it does not change the social order; technology, education, law and media are sources of social change.

s: Those who have similar incomes or are similar in other respects like age, occupation, education are called
src: Civil Services (Preliminary) 1998
x: People of similar income, occupation and education form social classes (options A and C are identical).

s: Which of the following is not the basis for social stratification?
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: Caste, class, gender, age, race, ethnicity, education, occupation, income and power are bases of stratification; language is not.

s: The system of caste conversion is an example of what?
src: APPSC Sociology General Studies 2000
x: The stem is garbled ('caste conversion'); the options mix Polanyi's forms of exchange with 'antagonism', and caste-based exchange is read by some as reciprocity and by others as redistribution, so no option can be settled.

s: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with the special provision with respect to the State of Andhra Pradesh?
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: Article 371D (32nd Amendment, 1973, after the Six-Point Formula) gives special provisions for Andhra Pradesh (and Telangana) on equitable opportunities in public employment and education.

s: Which of the following practices leads to social exclusion?
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: Separate (segregated) special schools keep blind children apart from mainstream schooling, so they lead to exclusion; inclusive education in ordinary schools is the alternative. Segregation is one of the practices of exclusion.

s:
Which of the following is/are not correct about 'SHe-box'?

a. It is an online complaint management system for registering complaints related to sexual harassment at workplace.

b. This portal is an initiative by the Government of India to provide a single window access to every woman, irrespective of her work status, whether working in organised or unorganised, private or public sector.
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Both are correct: SHe-Box is an online complaint system for workplace sexual harassment, open to every woman whatever her work status – organised or unorganised, private or public.

s:
Match List-1 with List-2 and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-1 (Freedom Fighters):

a. Bhikaji Cama

b. Sarojini Naidu

c. Kamala Nehru

d. Vijayalaxmi Pandit
List-2 (Honours):

1. The first woman President of UN General Assembly

2. The Delhi Beauty

3. The Nightingale of India

4. Mother of the Indian Revolution
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: Bhikaji Cama – 'Mother of the Indian Revolution'; Sarojini Naidu – 'Nightingale of India'; Vijayalakshmi Pandit – first woman President of the UN General Assembly (1953); Kamala Nehru takes the remaining 'Delhi Beauty' by elimination.

s: Which one of the following is not among the five women empowerment components given by the United Nations?
at: Restrictions for women to have access to resources
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: The UN's five components of women's empowerment are: sense of self-worth; the right to have and determine choices; the right to ACCESS opportunities and resources; the right to control their own lives; and the ability to influence social change. 'Restrictions' on access is the opposite.

s: Which of the following is a Government of Andhra Pradesh scheme to provide LPG connections to women of BPL families?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: AP's Deepam scheme (1999) gave LPG connections to women (DWCRA/BPL) families; 'Deepam-2' (November 2024) now gives three free cylinders a year.

s: Under the Scheme for Adolescent Girls (SAGs) which of the following marks the day of their general health checkup?
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Under SABLA / the Scheme for Adolescent Girls, a Kishori Diwas is held at the Anganwadi (quarterly) for the general health check-up and referral of adolescent girls.

s: Read about "Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan" (RUSA) and identify wrong statement
at: It is recommended by National Education Commission
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: RUSA (2013) funds State higher-education institutions; the statement that it was recommended by the National Education Commission is the wrong one.

s: Out of under mentioned statements, which one is not correct, in regard to changes brought about and necessitated by RTE - Act 2009 about current status of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA)?
at: It is mandatory on the Government of India to bring the early childhood care and education under umbrella of SSA
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Early childhood care and education is under Art. 45 (DPSP) and outside the RTE Act, so it is not mandatory on the Government of India to bring ECCE under SSA – the incorrect statement.

s: Which of the following is the component of "Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan"?
at: National Programme for Education of Girls at Elementary Level
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: NPEGEL (National Programme for Education of Girls at Elementary Level) was a component of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan.

s: Which one is not correct in regard to Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA)?
at: Ensuring accessibility, availability and affordability to quality secondary education is a constitutional commitment of the Government of India.
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: Only elementary education (6-14) is a constitutional commitment (Art. 21A); calling universal access to quality secondary education a constitutional commitment is the incorrect RMSA statement.

s: Which statement is not associated with Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA)?
at: It aims to provide universal education for all children between 6 - 16 years age group.
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: RMSA is for secondary education; 'universal education for all children aged 6-16' is not an RMSA aim (6-14 is RTE).

s:
Identify the specific interventions introduced for Universalization of education (elementary). To answer, choose the correct option from the code given below:

a. Mid-day meals

b. Distribution of free books and uniforms

c. Distribution of free laptops

d. Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan

e. Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya
at: Code: a, b, d and e
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: Mid-day meals, free books and uniforms, SSA and KGBVs are interventions for universal elementary education; free laptops are not – code a, b, d and e.

s: Which statement is not associated with RMSA (Rashtriya Madhyamika Shiksha Abhiyan)?
at: It aims to provide universal education for all children between 6-16 age group
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: RMSA aims at secondary education; 'universal education for all children aged 6-16' is not associated with it.

s: Which one is not correct about the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA)?
at: After the implementation of RTE - Act 2009, the Government of India affords whole expenses of SSA
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: SSA costs are shared between the Centre and the States even after the RTE Act, so 'the Government of India affords the whole expense of SSA' is the incorrect statement.

s: Which one statement distinguish NPE 1986, from NPE 1968 in regard to universalisation of elementary education
at: It added another goal to the universalisation of elementary education, attainment of minimum level of learning (MLL)
src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Assistant Telugu Translator 2019
x: NPE 1986 added the goal of minimum levels of learning (MLL) to universal elementary education, stressing quality beyond enrolment.

s: Which of the following homes is not the part of the Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act of 2000?
src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Assistant Telugu Translator 2019
x: The JJ Act 2000 provided Observation, Special, Children's and Shelter Homes; a Protective Home belongs to the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act.

s: Which of the following is not a service of ICDS Programme?
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: A 100-day job guarantee belongs to MGNREGA, not ICDS, whose six services are nutrition, pre-school, health education, immunisation, check-up and referral.

s: Which of the following is a characteristic of the 'authoritarian parenting' style?
at: Parent strictly controls all aspects of the child's life
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Authoritarian parenting means high control and strict obedience with little warmth or explanation.
